title: Gold Nanostar Synthesis with a Silver Seed Mediated Growth Method
protocol: Prepare a stock solution of silver nitrate by mixing an arbitrary mass with 10 mL of deionized water.
Calculate the molarity of the silver nitrate solution.
Keep the silver nitrate solution in a dark place to isolate it from light.
Add 14.7 mg of sodium citrate tribasic to 10 mL of deionized water to make a 5 mM solution.
Shake the vial until the powder is dissolved.
Add 15.1 mg of sodium borohydride to another vial with 10 mL of deionized water to make a 40 mM solution.
Close the sodium borohydride vial immediately.
Place the sodium borohydride solution in a beaker with ice and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
From the stock silver nitrate solution, prepare 10 mL at 0.25 mM.
Place a stirring magnet in the vial of 0.25 mM silver nitrate and start stirring.
Add 0.25 mL of the sodium citrate tribasic solution to the stirring solution.
After 15 minutes, remove the sodium borohydride solution from the refrigerator.
Using a pipette, add 0.4 mL of the sodium borohydride solution to the stirring solution in one quick stroke.
Stir the solution for 5 minutes after adding the sodium borohydride solution.
At t1 = 20 min, stop stirring and remove the magnet from the vial.
Keep the silver seed solution in a dark place at room temperature without closing the vial.
Do not close the vial to allow evaporation of excess reducing agent.
Let the solution remain undisturbed for at least two hours before using.
Prepare 80 mM ascorbic acid by adding 140 mg to 10 mL of DI water.
Calculate the molarity of 10 mL of gold chloride solution.
Keep the gold chloride solution isolated from light.
Prepare 20 mL of 50 mM cetyltrimethylammonium bromide (CTAB) by adding 364 mg to a vial with 20 mL of DI water.
Start stirring on a warm plate at 30°C after CTAB powder is completely dissolved and the solution becomes transparent.
Add ascorbic acid solution to the CTAB solution to obtain a final molarity of 4.9x10^-2 mM.
At t2 = 1 min, add gold chloride solution to the mixture to obtain a final molarity of 0.25 mM.
At t2 = 2 min, add 0.1 mL of ascorbic acid solution to the mixture.
The solution will turn colorless at this step.
At t2 = 2 min 20 sec, add 0.05 mL of silver seeds to the mixture.
Stir the suspension for 15 min; it will initially turn blue and then brown.
Stop stirring at t2 = 17 min, remove the magnet, and keep the suspension at room temperature for 24 hours.
Sonicate the suspension for 2 minutes.
Centrifuge the suspension for 5 min at 730 rcf.
Remove most of the supernatant with a pipette carefully, avoiding the nanostars on the tube wall.
Add DI water to the tube containing the nanostars.
Sonicate the mixture for 2 min.
Centrifuge the suspension for 3 min at 460 rcf.
Remove most of the supernatant with a pipette carefully.
Add DI water to the suspension.
Centrifuge the suspension for 3 min at 380 rcf.
Remove most of the supernatant with a pipette carefully.
The nanostars are now ready for imaging, spectroscopy, or experimentation.
Measure the absorption spectra of silver seeds using an Olis Cary-14 spectrophotometer.
Record the peak absorption of silver seeds at 400 nm.
Measure the absorption spectra of gold nanostars using an Olis Cary-14 spectrophotometer.
Determine the peak absorption range for gold nanostars between 800 nm and 850 nm.
